title: Program Kit Keycloak TLS and generated-profile conformance correction
intent: Define a separately approved correction to PKHT-W100 so the disposable Aspire-backed Keycloak fixture proves the actual HTTPS-only generated security profiles without global trust mutation, permissive certificate validation, provider-specific semantic leakage, or false claims caused by a Windows DCP control-plane blocker.
scope: Runtime-only creation of one fixture-owned ephemeral certificate authority, Keycloak server certificate, and private key inside an exact disposable execution root after explicit fixture-execution authority.

Read-only mounting of the exact server certificate and private key into the pinned Keycloak container, HTTPS-only provider startup, and exact issuer, metadata, token-endpoint, hostname, and certificate-name alignment.
Isolated trust of the exact fixture authority by generated test hosts, generated browser verification, and direct adversarial protocol clients without machine or user trust-store mutation.
End-to-end execution of the actual Program Kit confidential OIDC, public-browser OIDC with PKCE, JWT resource-server, OAuth client-credentials, and RFC 8693 token-exchange projections.
Cross-platform integration packaging that supports a Linux container execution environment while preserving separately classified Windows Aspire DCP control-plane blocker evidence.
Deterministic offline fixture generation, exact package and image evidence, redacted outcome evidence, bounded teardown, and proof that no runtime private material survives.
nonGoals: No change to the exact approved host-tooling 1.3.0 design or implementation-plan bytes and no retroactive expansion of their approval.
No HTTP authority, HTTP metadata, RequireHttpsMetadata=false, arbitrary loopback-certificate acceptance, Playwright IgnoreHTTPSErrors, or other weakening presented as secure-profile conformance.
No machine-root or current-user certificate install, trust, removal, cleanup, repair, or mutation.
No Winsock, IP, DNS, proxy, firewall, route, network-adapter, Docker-network, or operating-system network configuration.
No replacement of the Aspire-backed requirement with direct Docker, Testcontainers, Docker Compose, or a Program Kit-owned orchestrator.
No Program Kit runtime dependency on a Dev Container, Aspire CLI, external repository, external runtime wrapper, or provider-specific domain model.
No production certificate lifecycle, production Keycloak provisioning, backup, migration, administration, health policy, or deployment meaning.
No claim that a successful raw protocol exchange alone proves a generated application profile.
assumptions: The approved host-tooling 1.3.0 review set remains authoritative and implementation of this correction requires both its active approval and a separate approval of this exact review set.

The pinned Aspire.Hosting.Keycloak adapter exposes Keycloak development transport over HTTP by default, so an explicit fixture-owned TLS specialization is required to satisfy the existing HTTPS-only Program Kit profiles.

The fixture can generate certificate material at authorized runtime with .NET platform cryptography without adding a new runtime package, certificate store, centralized secret provider, or durable secret artifact.
The Keycloak image supports explicit PEM certificate and private-key files and an HTTPS-only listener through exact reviewed environment configuration.

The generated browser verifier can use an isolated browser trust boundary for the exact fixture authority; inability to establish exact trust fails the browser proof rather than enabling a global HTTPS-error bypass.

A Linux container may host the integration proof when the Windows Aspire DCP control plane fails before resource creation; environment selection changes verification location, not Program Kit semantics.
Raw protocol vectors remain useful additive evidence for negative cases, but the acceptance claim requires generated consumers to perform the selected roles.

sourceTruthAuthorities.governs: The human-requested corrective scope, rejected alternatives, safety boundaries, and new approval boundary.
The existing provider-neutral security profiles, secret boundaries, Aspire and Keycloak projection ownership, and HTTPS requirements that this correction may not weaken.
The W100 required outcomes, allowed edits, execution authority, verification, and stop conditions retained by the correction.

domains.purpose: Own universal deterministic development contracts, projections, conformance mechanics, and exact provider adapters without owning consumer-domain meaning.

vocabulary.meaning: Certificate authority, server certificate, and private-key material created only for one explicitly started disposable fixture, stored only under its exact runtime root, trusted only through isolated test processes, and destroyed during teardown.
Conformance evidence produced by executing the actual generated Program Kit role projection rather than only emulating its protocol calls in test code.
A failure below generated resource creation that prevents a selected execution environment from running the fixture and neither proves nor disproves provider/profile behavior.

semanticModels.meaning: The runtime-only certificate identities, allowed filesystem ownership, provider listener configuration, isolated trust bindings, teardown duties, and redacted evidence needed for one exact Keycloak fixture execution.
semanticModels.invariants: Provider HTTP is disabled for the proof; private material is never generated during deterministic source generation, committed, logged, packaged, or retained; trust is exact and process-isolated; every owned TLS file is removed during bounded teardown.

semanticModels.meaning: The role-by-role conformance composition joining exact generated confidential OIDC, public-browser OIDC, JWT resource-server, client-credentials, and token-exchange consumers to the pinned provider fixture.
semanticModels.invariants: HTTPS metadata remains required; actual generated consumers participate; direct protocol vectors are additive only; issuer, audience, scopes, token kinds, PKCE, state, nonce, signatures, lifetimes, replay, storage, and adverse paths fail closed.

components.compatibilityBoundary: Exact Keycloak image, Aspire integration, PEM configuration surface, certificate algorithm/profile, hostname, ports, runtime-root layout, trust mechanism, and teardown behavior.

components.purpose: Run the exact generated Program Kit security-role projections against the disposable TLS-enabled fixture and retain only bounded redacted outcomes.
components.compatibilityBoundary: Exact generated-profile revisions, test-host topology, browser engine selection, adversarial matrix, environment classification, and evidence schema.

artifactDecisions.requestedOutcome: Represent the separately reviewed W100 TLS and generated-profile proof correction as a validated canonical design.

executableBehavior.rationale: The design grants no implementation, fixture-execution, provider, certificate, browser, container, or network authority.

valueLifecycle.rationale: The design is schema-validated, compared with its exact parent artifacts and intent, and digest-bound to a separate implementation plan.

agentRetrieval.rationale: The review set is addressed through explicit repository paths.

agentProcedure.rationale: No capability, wrapper, hook, watcher, or autonomous procedure is created.

humanCommunication.audience: The human Program Kit architecture reviewer and implementers.
humanCommunication.decisionAuthorityBoundary: Only explicit human approval of the exact canonical design and implementation-plan digests authorizes implementation; fixture execution remains separately human-started.
humanCommunication.rationale: The correction changes security-sensitive fixture and conformance behavior.

generatedNavigation.rationale: No generated navigation artifact is needed for this bounded correction.

governance.provenancePolicy: The exact corrective intent and approved host-tooling 1.3.0 design and plan are named; implementation observations do not retroactively become architecture authority.
governance.digestPolicy: The review manifest binds exact design and plan bytes; any change requires revalidation, new digests, and a new human decision.
governance.compatibilityPolicy: Changing HTTPS requirements, trust isolation, private-material lifetime, generated-profile participation, Aspire backing, evidence semantics, or environment classification requires a new reviewed design version.
governance.migrationPolicy: The correction replaces only unapproved W100 checkpoint behavior; completed 1.3.0 work units remain untouched and W110 cannot close until the corrected W100 passes.

dataHandling.redactionPolicy: The design contains no credentials, tokens, cookies, claims, private keys, certificate identifiers, provider payloads, or machine-specific paths.
dataHandling.externalizationPolicy: Only the committed review artifacts and exact digests may be shared.
dataHandling.ephemeralDataPolicy: Runtime certificates, keys, secrets, provider state, browser state, logs, DCP data, and local paths remain outside the design.

artifactDecisions.rationale: A separately governed schema instance preserves the immutable parent approval while making the security correction exact and reviewable.

security.policy: The fixture must satisfy the existing HTTPS-only Program Kit profiles through exact runtime TLS and isolated trust, never by weakening profile validation.
guarantees: Keycloak metadata and token endpoints are HTTPS, provider HTTP is disabled for the proof, and exact issuer, hostname, certificate names, algorithms, lifetimes, audience, scopes, and token kinds remain fail closed.
Direct clients and browsers trust only the fixture-owned authority through process-isolated configuration.
exclusions: No arbitrary loopback certificate callback, disabled certificate validation, insecure metadata, browser-wide HTTPS-error bypass, or HTTP-equivalence claim.

authority.policy: Design approval, implementation approval, fixture execution, provider startup, browser startup, and any environment preparation are distinct human authority boundaries.
guarantees: Installing the package or generating fixture artifacts grants no execution authority.
exclusions: No design, generated artifact, environment variable, or prior execution silently starts infrastructure or expands authority.

secrets.policy: Passwords, client secrets, tokens, cookies, private keys, and browser state exist only inside the authorized fixture execution and exact owned root or process.
guarantees: TLS private material is created after execution starts, mounted read-only, never emitted by deterministic generation, and removed during teardown.
Durable evidence contains classifications, revisions, digests of reviewed public/provider inputs, and outcome states only.
exclusions: No raw secret, private key, token, cookie, certificate identifier, secret reference identity, absolute runtime path, provider log, or DCP configuration is durable evidence.

persistence.policy: Only deterministic source, schemas, locks, reviewed public version evidence, tests, and redacted outcomes are durable.
guarantees: Fixture runtime roots, certificates, keys, container state, browser profiles, traces, videos, HAR files, cookies, and tokens are absent after successful teardown.
exclusions: No persistent Keycloak volume, certificate store, browser profile, provider backup, or migration artifact.

failure.policy: TLS, generated-profile, provider, DCP, environment, browser, and teardown failures are separately classified and cannot be promoted as successful conformance.
guarantees: Missing or substituted certificates, HTTP fallback, disabled validation, non-generated consumers, provider drift, unsupported browser trust, residual state, and redaction failure fail W100.
A DCP failure before resource creation is recorded as an environment blocker and does not trigger source, TLS, trust, network, or provider weakening.
exclusions: No automatic fallback from HTTPS to HTTP, Aspire to direct Docker, generated profiles to raw protocol emulation, or Linux to host network repair.

concurrency.policy: Each execution owns a unique exact runtime root, certificate identities, ports, browser state, and container resources.
guarantees: Parallel or stale fixture roots cannot share private material, state, or teardown ownership.
exclusions: No shared mutable certificate cache, global browser profile, fixed private key, or ambient provider state.

cancellation.policy: Cancellation stops further assertions and always enters bounded owned-state teardown.
guarantees: Cancellation does not retain or promote partial protocol, browser, certificate, or provider evidence.
exclusions: No claim that cancellation can repair or roll back host, Docker, or provider state outside the exact fixture ownership boundary.

observability.policy: Evidence is redacted, non-authoritative, bounded, and separated by DCP, provider, generated-host, protocol, browser, and teardown phase.
guarantees: Evidence records exact public revisions and outcome classifications without credentials, token material, claims, private keys, certificate identifiers, absolute paths, raw provider output, or raw DCP configuration.
exclusions: No diagnostic signal becomes a security audit, authorization decision, provider administration record, or proof for a phase that did not execute.

compatibility.policy: Keycloak, Aspire integration, .NET, Playwright, browser, TLS algorithm/profile, generated security contracts, image, and execution-environment revisions are independently exact.
guarantees: A version or configuration change requires reviewed evidence and cannot silently change the secure-profile proof.
exclusions: No floating provider image, package, browser, certificate algorithm, platform image, Aspire CLI, or environment default.

scenarios.actor: Explicitly human-started Program Kit conformance profile
scenarios.intent: Prove every selected generated security role against one exact disposable TLS-enabled Keycloak provider fixture.
preconditions: The exact host-tooling 1.3.0 and corrective review-set approvals are active.
The integration environment satisfies the exact .NET, Aspire, container runtime, image, browser, and package selections.
steps: Generate deterministic realm, AppHost, generated consumer hosts/clients, locks, schemas, and secret-free configuration.
Create fixture-owned TLS material under a unique runtime root and bind exact isolated trust without touching host stores.
Start the pinned Aspire AppHost and Keycloak HTTPS resource, rejecting HTTP fallback.
Run generated confidential OIDC, public-browser PKCE, JWT API, client-credentials, and token-exchange consumers plus additive adversarial vectors.
Cancel or complete, tear down all owned processes, containers, browser state, certificates, keys, and runtime files, then emit redacted phase outcomes.
outcomes: The actual generated Program Kit profiles pass against a substitutable provider without provider-specific domain meaning or weakened HTTPS rules.
No sensitive or fixture-owned runtime material remains.
failureOutcomes: Any TLS bypass, HTTP fallback, non-generated role emulation, profile mismatch, residual runtime material, provider drift, teardown failure, or redaction failure rejects conformance.

scenarios.intent: Separate an Aspire DCP environment failure from provider and generated-profile behavior without changing host networking or weakening the fixture.
preconditions: The selected environment fails before Keycloak resource creation.
steps: Classify the last completed phase and sanitize bounded diagnostics.
Tear down the exact owned process and filesystem state.
Record an environment-blocker outcome and select a separately authorized supported Linux container environment for a later execution.
outcomes: The Windows-host blocker is truthful and does not become false provider failure or false conformance.
No operating-system network or certificate repair is attempted.
failureOutcomes: Changing system networking, trust stores, provider transport, validation policy, or Aspire backing exceeds the design and stops work.

statusClaims.claim: The corrective design is ready for validation and human review; it does not approve implementation or fixture execution.
